protocol.description: This protocol allows privileged clients to manage window layering, relative stacking orders within layers, exclusive edge reservations for shell components (taskbars), and activation without tokens.

interface.name: wex_window_manager_v1

description.summary: manager interface for privileged window controls

interface.description: Allows obtaining a wex_window_v1 interface for an xdg_toplevel. Only advertised to privileged clients on the wex-shell socket.

description.summary: create a wex_window_v1 from an xdg_toplevel

interface.name: wex_window_v1
interface.description: Provides operations for stacking, layering, shell edge reservation, and direct activation.

entry.name: desktop
entry.summary: below everything, not in window cycling

entry.name: shell
entry.summary: above topmost, not in window cycling

description.summary: place above sibling in the same layer
place below sibling in the same layer
lower to the bottom of its layer
give keyboard focus and raise within its layer

event.name: handle
event.description: Sent once when the object is created. This compositor-generated token identifies the window until its view or control object is destroyed. Privileged clients may share it across connections. Treat it as opaque.

request.name: place_above_handle

description.summary: place above a shared sibling handle

request.description: Like place_above, but accepts a sibling from another privileged client. Unknown, stale, self, or different-layer handles are harmless no-ops.

request.name: place_below_handle

description.summary: place below a shared sibling handle

request.description: Like place_below, but accepts a sibling from another privileged client. Unknown, stale, self, or different-layer handles are harmless no-ops.

request.name: restore
request.description: Clear minimization without activating or raising the window. Use activate instead when the client also wants to give keyboard focus.
